extracted.intended_audience: newsroom editors, editorial managers, digital journalists, and media/journalism researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how news organizations should collect and use audience data and metrics to inform editorial decisions, balancing real-time quantitative signals with audience research and traditional editorial judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data informs but does not dominate editorial decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Best practice: data informs but does not dominate editorial decisions. Newsrooms use a mix of data and judgment to make editorial choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine quantitative signals with audience research and editorial judgment; avoid allowing metrics alone to determine coverage or to undermine editorial mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real-time dashboards (clicks, time-on-page)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of real-time dashboards showing metrics such as clicks and time-on-page to monitor immediate performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for short-term monitoring and responsiveness; risk: privileging short-term attention metrics over deeper quality measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience research (panels, surveys)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematic audience research methods (panels, surveys) to understand audience preferences and needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides contextual and explanatory insight beyond surface metrics; complements dashboards by revealing motivations and unmet needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial judgment (traditional news values)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply traditional editorial values and professional judgment alongside data signals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure accountability, public-service obligations, and long-term mission are not displaced by short-term metrics; serve as a corrective when data suggests low-value but high-click stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description (analytics stage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Description — what happened (e.g., clicks, sources).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First-stage analytics: collect and report raw or aggregate metrics to understand outcomes and behavior patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnosis (analytics stage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagnosis — why it happened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second-stage analytics: analyze causation, drivers, and contextual factors behind performance to inform learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prescription (analytics stage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prescription — what should we do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-stage analytics: translate insights into concrete editorial actions, experiments, or strategy changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page views — gross attention
rubrics_metrics.description: Page views measure gross attention paid to a story or page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for scale; risk: incentivizes click-chasing and may not reflect quality or depth of engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique visitors
rubrics_metrics.description: Unique visitors as a metric of audience reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates breadth of audience exposure; combine with engagement metrics to assess value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time on page — engagement depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Time on page used as a proxy for engagement depth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longer dwell time can indicate deeper engagement or interest; interpret carefully (e.g., accidental long times vs. attentive reading).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scroll depth — reading completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Scroll depth as a measure of how far users progress through content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps assess whether content formats and lengths are being consumed; can inform formatting and editorial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing — virality
rubrics_metrics.description: Sharing metrics measure social spread and virality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals resonance and amplification potential; consider the quality and context of shares (e.g., critical vs. endorsing shares).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments — engagement intensity
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments as an indicator of engagement intensity and audience interaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High comment volumes can indicate strong interest but may also reflect controversy or moderation burdens; assess sentiment and constructiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeat visits — loyalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeat visits used to measure audience loyalty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track frequency and patterns of return to evaluate retention and habit formation; valuable for long-term audience strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscriber conversion — quality signal
rubrics_metrics.description: Subscriber conversion used as a qualitative signal of valuable audience relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversions indicate perceived value and willingness to pay; prioritize strategies that foster conversion without eroding editorial standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source of traffic — discoverability
rubrics_metrics.description: Source of traffic indicates how audiences find content (search, social, direct).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to understand discoverability and partnership/opportunity channels; tailor formats and headlines to dominant referral sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic prioritization based on past performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize topics for coverage based on historical audience performance data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can improve short-term traffic but risk narrowing coverage to proven winners; balance with mission-driven journalism and investigative work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline A/B testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Run A/B tests on headlines to optimize clickthrough and engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use responsibly to learn which wording better communicates while avoiding sensationalism or misleading framing; monitor downstream quality metrics (dwell, conversions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-of-day targeting for posts
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule posts at optimal times of day based on audience behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage temporal patterns to maximize reach and engagement; be mindful of news cycles and editorial timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format experimentation (lists, video, longform)
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiment with different content formats (lists, video, longform) to see what performs with audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use experiments to find format-performance fit; avoid over-optimizing for formats that undermine depth or accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience segmentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Segment audiences to tailor content, headlines, and distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps personalize and target content for different cohorts (e.g., casual vs. loyal readers); ensure segmentation doesn’t silo audiences or compromise journalistic standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative metrics vs. quality (tension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tension between quantitative metrics (clicks) and journalistic quality (depth, accountability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize trade-offs; implement checks so metrics do not erode investigative work or standards of accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term performance vs. long-term mission (tension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tension between chasing short-term performance and maintaining long-term editorial mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect long-term investments (investigations, beat reporting) even when metrics favor short-term sensational pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience demand vs. audience needs (tension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tension between giving audiences what they click on (demand) and serving their information needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance appealing content with journalism that educates and holds power to account; use audience research to identify unmet needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freelance/PR-driven topics can undermine independence (tension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Observation that freelance or PR-driven topics may generate clicks but risk undermining editorial independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of monetization or sourcing pressures that favor PR material; maintain sourcing standards and editorial integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicted clickability as a news value
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of predicted clickability as an implicit new news value influencing story selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat predicted clickability as one input among many; safeguard against making it the dominant criterion for newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicted dwell time
rubrics_metrics.description: Using predictions of dwell time to assess likely depth of audience engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate dwell-time forecasts into format and headline decisions while validating predictions against actual engagement quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicted social spread
rubrics_metrics.description: Predicting social spread to evaluate a story's potential to be shared and amplified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider amplification potential when planning distribution and follow-ups; check for potential reputational risks associated with viral framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicted subscriber retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Using analytics to predict which content will retain or convert subscribers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize content strategies that demonstrably contribute to long-term subscriber relationships rather than transient clicks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format performance fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessing whether a content format is appropriate to achieve desired metric outcomes (e.g., lists vs. longform).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match format to audience behaviors and editorial goals; iterate through experiments and use combined metrics (engagement + retention) to judge success.
